title: CSS Colours
summary: Opens the CSS properties section with colour: background-color versus color, named colours, and hex codes (with a pointer to Color Hunt for palettes). Ends with a five-step exercise colouring a page with named colours and hex codes.

concepts.heading: Property and value recap
points: A CSS declaration is property, colon, value. The property says what to change; the value says what to set it to.
background-color fills the area behind an element. Applied to body (the html content wrapper in practice), it colours the whole page.
color sets the colour of the text inside the element, not its background. Check MDN when unsure which property controls what.
background-color works on any element: it fills the element's own box (e.g. an h1's block area), not just the body.

concepts.heading: Named colours
points: CSS defines a built-in list of colour keywords such as cornflowerblue, cadetblue, dimgrey, olivedrab, antiquewhite, whitesmoke, darkseagreen.
The full list is on MDN (search 'MDN named color'). The table shows each name next to its hex code and a swatch.
The 'CSS Level 1/2/3' labels in that table only record when each name was added historically; ignore them when choosing.
Usage: copy the keyword and paste it as the value, no quotes, no hash.

concepts.heading: Hex codes and custom palettes
points: Named colours are limited, so for a custom look use a palette tool. The lecture recommends colorhunt.co: free designer-made palettes of several colours (background tone, heading tone, accent tones).
Palette tools give hex codes like #5D3891 rather than names. A hex code is a compact way of writing an RGB colour.
RGB: a colour is a mix of red, green and blue, each from 0 to 255. The example purple is 93 red, 56 green, 145 blue; its hex form is the same three numbers written in base 16.
Hex format: # followed by six hex digits, two each for red, green, blue (#RRGGBB).
In code a hex value goes exactly where a name would: color: #faf8f1;
(Extra) Hex digits run 0-9 then a-f, so 00 is none and ff is full (255). #000000 is black, #ffffff is white. Also valid: three-digit shorthand like #fff, rgb(), hsl().
Pick colours that work as a set: one for the background, one for headings, one for subtitles, plus accents.

task.name: 6.1 CSS Colors
task.starting_point: index.html has a page with just an h1 and an h2 (Hello / World) and no colour; the preview is black text on white.
task.goal: Add CSS so the page matches goal.png: a coloured page background, a coloured h1 with a background, and a coloured h2 with a background. The h1 must use named colours; the h2 must use hex codes, to practise both notations.
steps: Set the body background-color to antiquewhite.
Set the h1 text colour (color) to whitesmoke.
Set the h1 background-color to darkseagreen.
Set the h2 text colour to the hex value #faf8f1.
Set the h2 background-color to the hex value #c58940. Save and check the preview against the goal image.
task.expected_result: Antique-white page; h1 pale text on a sage-green band; h2 cream text on a tan/gold band.

pitfalls: Using color when you meant background-color (or the reverse): color only affects text.
Forgetting the # before a hex code, which makes the declaration invalid and ignored.
Needing 'lateral thinking': background-color is allowed on h1/h2 too, not only on body.
Reference repo note: it carries an author footer ('Made with...') that is not part of the exercise; ignore it.

playground.coverage: Tasks and solution match the exercise exactly (antiquewhite body, whitesmoke on darkseagreen h1, hex h2). Explore demo has colour pickers with a live CSS readout; notes cover named, hex, rgb, rgba.
gaps_and_ideas: Notes recommend coolors.co, but the lecture uses colorhunt.co; mention both or correct it.
Add the lecture's point that color = text and background-color = fill, as a side-by-side explore toggle.
Explain hex as three RGB channels: show an explore demo with three 0-255 sliders producing both rgb() and the hex string (the 93/56/145 purple example).
Add a link or mini-table to MDN's named-colour list and a task to swap one named colour for its hex equivalent.
